제목: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning
저자: Yiran Lin; Ye Deng; Ziqi Pan; Yongan Yu; Alexandra I. Cristea
초록: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly explored as collaborative learning partners in mathematics education, yet it remains unclear what makes an AI recognizable as a peer. This study examines how domain experts perceive and interact with an adaptive LLM-based peer agent combining a Big Five-informed persona with motivational state modulation for collaborative mathematics problem solving. Through thematic analysis of expert interviews, we identify conditions shaping peer perceptions, including emotional safety, shared control, and collaborative reasoning. Participants primarily judged the AI through its social behavior rather than mathematical capabilities. The AI was perceived more as a peer when it created a non-judgmental space, engaged in tentative reasoning, displayed appropriate imperfection, and respected participants' pace. Conversely, blind agreement and over-instruction reduced trust and shifted perceptions toward a tutor role. Based on these findings, we propose human-centered design dimensions for AI peer agents to guide future peer-oriented learning systems.
상세페이지_제목: Exploring AI Peer in Collaborative Mathematics Learning

제목: What the submission does not show: Complexifying cognitive offloading in students' mathematical work with LLMs
저자: Igor' Kontorovich; Miriam N. Wallach
초록: A common concern is that using large language models (LLMs) lets students offload mathematical work that tasks are designed to elicit. Yet such claims often rest on outcomes (e.g., submitted solutions), rather than on evidence of students' work with LLMs. We followed 23 first-year linear algebra students as they solved three differently designed homework tasks with LLMs. Drawing on self-regulated learning and choice-affluent environments, we interpreted each of 429 prompts as a trace of a regulatory event and compared 59 chatlogs with the problem solutions the students submitted. Prompts formed five structures, casting the LLM mainly as a solver, explainer, or validator. The mix of structures shifted across the tasks, and ten of the 15 students who completed all three tasks changed their dominant structure. Most final submissions stayed close to LLM output, including those that followed exchanges in which students had explained, conjectured, and checked their own ideas. We conclude that an LLM-aided submission is not a trustworthy marker of students' offloading of the mathematical work, and that offloading needs to be examined in each regulatory space and part by part rather than as a whole.
상세페이지_제목: What the submission does not show: Complexifying cognitive offloading in students' mathematical work with LLMs

제목: STEPwise: Supporting Teachers in Diagnosing Students' Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills through LLM-Generated Questions and Rubric
저자: Yoonsu Kim; Hayeon Doh; Eunhye Kim; Jinho Son; Juho Kim
초록: Problem-solving is central to mathematics education. However, diagnosing where students' reasoning breaks down requires individualized probing and consistent criteria that teachers cannot sustain at classroom scale. We introduce STEP (STage-based Evaluation of Problem-solving skills), co-designed with six mathematics education experts, which operationalizes problem-solving as four stages and eight diagnostic sub-skills. By specifying what evidence to elicit and assess at each stage, STEP enables an LLM pipeline to generate stage-specific questions and rubrics for any math word problem, reducing the manual design of diagnostic materials. An expert review (N=8) assessed the pedagogical validity of the generated materials and informed STEPwise, a teacher-in-the-loop system for diagnostic material generation and process-level assessment. In a classroom study with 5 teachers and 64 students, STEPwise helped teachers and students locate reasoning breakdowns and supported students in reflecting on their reasoning. Together, STEP and STEPwise offer a structured approach to fine-grained diagnosis at classroom scale.
상세페이지_제목: STEPwise: Supporting Teachers in Diagnosing Students' Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills through LLM-Generated Questions and Rubric

제목: Theory of Situations
저자: Marie-Jeanne Perrin-Glorian; Claire Margolinas
초록: Guy Brousseau began developing the theory of situations in the 1960s, with the ambition of building an experimental epistemology of mathematics. Over the decades, the theory has been structured, consolidated and extended, drawing on the contributions of numerous researchers. It is now recognized as one of the ''genuine ground theories'' in mathematics education. In this chapter, we will describe the foundations and reasons for the existence of this theory, its systemic approach to teaching and learning issues, its current architecture, which articulates a theory of mathematical situations and a theory of didactic situations, and its key concepts, as well as its functions, particularly its predictive and explanatory functions. We will illustrate this presentation with an example in geometry that also highlights the role played by the didactic engineering methodology in this theory and related work.
상세페이지_제목: Theory of Situations

제목: Sensemaking of physics equations: Rationale, conceptualization, and core strategies
저자: Julia Hofmann; Pascal Klein; Andreas Müller; Josefine Neuhaus
초록: In physics instruction, equations are often treated primarily as tools for obtaining numerical results. Yet physicists also use them to describe dependencies, explain why those dependencies hold, predict what happens in new situations, test expressions against physical knowledge, and explore consequences that are not immediately apparent. Although such uses appear throughout the physics education literature, they have not been brought together in a systematic account, and the terminology used to describe them remains inconsistent. Drawing on research in mathematics education on symbol sense and the function concept, we distinguish six epistemic functions of physics equations: calculating, describing, explaining, predicting, evaluating, and exploring. We then characterize six strategies through which these functions can be realized: dimensional analysis, order of magnitude analysis, covariational analysis, special case analysis, limiting case analysis, and formal analogies, illustrating each with examples from introductory physics. To examine how these strategies are viewed within the discipline, we surveyed 31 physicists at one university faculty about five of the strategies. Respondents regarded the strategies as indispensable to physics, judged limiting case analysis to be more difficult for students than dimensional analysis, and reported that their own courses could devote more time to them. By distinguishing what physicists use equations for from the strategies by which they do so, the paper provides a vocabulary for sensemaking of physics equations and specifies what explicit instruction in these strategies involves.
상세페이지_제목: Sensemaking of physics equations: Rationale, conceptualization, and core strategies

제목: LeanSide: A Formally Verified Co-Reasoning System for Natural-language Proofs
저자: Chenjun Guo; Manooshree Patel; Arnav Mehta; Krishiv Kothari; Thomas Lu; Niels Voss; Rayna Bhattacharyya; Peter Donovan; Bjoern Hartmann; Gireeja Ranade
초록: Large language models are increasingly used as collaborators on deductive-reasoning tasks, but their outputs can hallucinate or pull users away from intended reasoning. Formal proof assistants provide machine-checked verification, but have a steep learning curve and require more granular reasoning than human written proofs. We explore an interface that combines these strengths, allowing users to write and revise free-form natural-language proofs while a verified backend checks their reasoning and returns feedback at the user's granularity. We study this interface in the context of undergraduate mathematics education by developing LeanSide, a formally verified co-reasoning system, which auto-formalizes student reasoning into Lean and informalizes verifier output into understandable feedback. We conducted user studies through classroom deployment and analyzed which system properties helped students make progress and which caused them to get stuck. We use these findings to derive design implications for using a formally verified backend in human-AI co-reasoning systems.
상세페이지_제목: LeanSide: A Formally Verified Co-Reasoning System for Natural-language Proofs

제목: Training Mathematicians in the Age of AI: Intellectual Agency, Cognitive Offloading, and the PhD Thesis
저자: Thomas Koberda
초록: Powerful artificial intelligence is weakening the traditional relationship between mathematical output and evidence of mathematical expertise. In particular, the production of an original theorem or a polished dissertation can no longer, by itself, certify the intellectual formation of its nominal author. I argue that graduate mathematical education should therefore be organized around the formation of intellectual agency: internal technical competence, mathematical judgment, understanding, and responsible participation in a shared intellectual culture. I distinguish productive from premature cognitive offloading, propose complementary independent and AI-augmented modes of training, and suggest a corresponding reformulation of the role of the PhD thesis and dissertation defense. More broadly, I argue that academic mathematics should understand itself increasingly as an institution for the reproduction and stewardship of human mathematical expertise rather than primarily as a mechanism for producing theorems.
상세페이지_제목: Training Mathematicians in the Age of AI: Intellectual Agency, Cognitive Offloading, and the PhD Thesis

제목: Comparing different approaches to the concept of determinant: the multiplicative approach is the best!
저자: Peteris Daugulis; Mikhail H Klin; Anita Sondore
초록: The determinant is traditionally introduced through permutation expansions, multilinearity, or recursive expansion formulas - approaches that, while rigorous, often obscure its conceptual significance. Instead, an approach is advocated wherein the determinant is defined via its natural characterization as a multiplicatice map on matrices, reflecting its role as a structural invariant of linear transformations under composition. This perspective defers combinatorial machinery until after the core properties are estaqblished, thereby lowering the cognitive barrier for students encountering the concept for the first time. The equivalence of this characterization with classical formulations is shown, and it is argued that this framework better aligns with the structural emphasis of m odern mathematical education.
상세페이지_제목: Comparing different approaches to the concept of determinant: the multiplicative approach is the best!

제목: Compartmental Epidemiological Models: Discussing Fundamental Elements via the SIR Model
저자: Ligia Liani Barz; Jose Rafael Santos Furlanetto; Fernando Deeke Sasse
초록: We present a didactic treatment of compartmental disease spread modeling centered on the SIR framework, aimed at mathematics education. Our focus is on how modeling choices encode transmission mechanisms and data-collection practices. We begin by stating the structural hypotheses of compartmental models, including population partitioning, homogeneous mixing, flow closure, and Markovian transitions. We then derive the basic SIR dynamic equations in both continuous-time (differential equations) and discrete-time (difference equations) settings. A key goal is to clarify the distinction between density-dependent and frequency-dependent transmission. We do this by constructing the force of infection from the contact rate, prevalence, and per-contact transmissibility while tracking units and interpretations. We go beyond the usual mass-balance SIR model by introducing the discrete Kermack-McKendrick perspective through the cumulative force of infection. This naturally leads to discrete SIR updates with an exponential escape probability term. We also derive Bernoulli-based exponential formulations for both density- and frequency-dependent transmission, interpret these probabilistically over observation intervals, and obtain the associated discrete infectivity kernel. This highlights how geometric infectious survival emerges from per-step removal. The paper includes reproducible, introductory-level Python code to implement the basic discrete SIR model, the continuous SIR model, and the exponential discrete variants. We provide instructors with an example of parameter estimation from prevalence data using least squares, along with guidance on interpretation and limitations. This framework is designed to help teachers integrate model assumptions, units, simulation, and inference in a coherent introduction to infectious disease modeling.
상세페이지_제목: Compartmental Epidemiological Models: Discussing Fundamental Elements via the SIR Model

제목: Mathematics Graduate Training in the Age of AI
저자: David Glickenstein
초록: Generative AI changes the conditions under which graduate mathematics is learned, assessed, written, and defended. The central claim of this paper is that mathematics graduate programs should respond to the moment by clarifying what graduate mathematics education is trying to teach and assess. In most ways, the goals of mathematics education have not changed. Rather, with changing tools it has become more essential than ever to make clear the goals of mathematical training. We use the term mathematical judgment to refer to the capacity to evaluate mathematics (e.g., claims, definitions, examples, proofs, analogies, computations, uses of tools, research directions) as mathematically sound, useful, well-posed, and appropriately justified. The recommendation is to center training on mathematical judgment, and we examine possible policies for graduate programs in Mathematics to this end.
상세페이지_제목: Mathematics Graduate Training in the Age of AI

제목: Extraction of different electronic contributions to transport properties of transition metals from first principles
저자: I. S. Galtsov; D. V. Minakov; P. R. Levashov
초록: Accurate transport properties calculations in transition metals require treating inter-orbital hybridization, which is often poorly captured by simplified single-band models. We propose an \textit{ab initio} approach combining maximally localized Wannier functions and the Allen's method to correctly account for this mixing, overcoming the artifacts inherent to the Souza-Marzari-Vanderbilt scheme. Our method enables efficient orbital-resolved analysis of transport spectral functions. Applied to face-centered cubic Pd and body-centered cubic Mo, we reveal universal scattering mechanisms despite distinct electronic structures in these metals. Crucially, the parallel addition of distinct scattering channels perfectly reproduces full Allen's method calculations, rigorously validating this decomposition. We show that the absence of a $d$-peak at Fermi level in Mo enhances $s$-$s$ scattering, while the same contribution to resistivity and electron thermal conductivity of Pd is close to the experimental data for Ag. Ultimately, the proposed method provides a universal and efficient tool for the microscopic analysis of electron-phonon scattering mechanisms in systems with strong hybridization between localized and delocalized electron states.
상세페이지_제목: Extraction of different electronic contributions to transport properties of transition metals from first principles

제목: Correlated quasiperiodicity enables efficient thermoelectric energy conversion
저자: Swaraj Biswas; Santanu K. Maiti
초록: We investigate a route to enhanced thermoelectric energy conversion in nanoscale systems by exploiting a correlated quasiperiodic energy landscape in a one-dimensional chain coupled to source and drain reservoirs. The considered modulation generates a highly non-uniform electronic transmission spectrum, providing favorable conditions for achieving a large thermoelectric figure of merit. By systematically tuning the incommensurability parameter, a variety of quasiperiodic configurations are explored, several of which yield high values of the figure of merit exceeding $2$. Electronic transport properties are evaluated within a tight-binding framework using the non-equilibrium Green's function formalism, while the thermoelectric coefficients, including electrical conductance, Seebeck coefficient, and electronic thermal conductance, are determined through the Landauer approach. The underlying quasiperiodic potential belongs to the Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) family and exhibits a weakly varying spatial profile, leading to transmission characteristics that are favorable for thermoelectric optimization. The influence of phonon thermal conductance on the overall energy-conversion efficiency is also analyzed in detail. For the sake of completeness, we also critically inspect the effect of conductor to electrode coupling and the coupling asymmetry on $ZT$. We also check the thermoelectric response of conventional AAH system and an elaborate comparison is made with our chosen quantum system. Our findings highlight the potential of correlated quasiperiodic nanostructures as promising candidates for efficient thermoelectric applications.
상세페이지_제목: Correlated quasiperiodicity enables efficient thermoelectric energy conversion

제목: Non-Hermitian impurity scattering in graphene: Boltzmann transport and thermoelectric response
저자: Juan A. Cañas; Daniel A. Bonilla; A. Martín-Ruiz
초록: We investigate charge and thermoelectric transport in monolayer graphene containing a dilute distribution of finite-range non-Hermitian scattering centers. The impurities are modeled as circular complex potentials, whose imaginary component describes local carrier loss or gain. By solving the Dirac scattering problem exactly within a partial-wave approach, we obtain the nonunitary scattering matrix and derive the transport and absorption cross sections, which separately characterize momentum relaxation and net carrier exchange with the environment. To connect the microscopic scattering problem with stationary transport, we formulate a semiclassical Boltzmann description in which an external reservoir compensates the equilibrium particle loss or gain. This leads to an effective relaxation time governed by both elastic momentum scattering and non-Hermitian flux exchange. Using the full energy-dependent relaxation time, we evaluate the Onsager coefficients and the resulting electrical conductivity, electronic thermal conductivity, Seebeck coefficient, Lorenz ratio, and electronic thermoelectric figure of merit. We find that weak gain increases the effective carrier lifetime and enhances both charge and heat conductivities, while absorption produces the opposite behavior. More importantly, gain enhances the magnitude of the thermopower and the electronic figure of merit, whereas loss suppresses them. The Lorenz ratio remains close to the Sommerfeld value, with non-Hermiticity mainly modifying its finite-temperature corrections. Our results show that non-Hermitian scattering provides an additional mechanism for controlling the energy dependence of carrier relaxation and, consequently, the thermoelectric response of graphene.
상세페이지_제목: Non-Hermitian impurity scattering in graphene: Boltzmann transport and thermoelectric response

제목: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
저자: Ariana M. Villegas-Suarez; Guido Freire; Sohan Venkatesh; Bartosz Cywiński
초록: Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) on harmful data in a narrow domain, such as bad medical advice, can make it broadly misaligned. How realistic this risk is remains unclear, since models are very rarely fine-tuned on explicitly harmful data in practice. In this work, we show that fine-tuning on data the model believes to be false but that has no harmful content, can also induce broad misalignment. Across mathematics, trivia, cooking and sports, the more strongly the model disbelieves the answers it is trained on, the more misaligned it becomes. In mathematics, misaligned answers rise from 4% to over 60% as the training answers become more wrong, with little loss of general capability. After fine-tuning, the model states the wrong answers but its multiple-choice probabilities still prefer the true ones, which suggests that misalignment comes from this internal inconsistency. We then study a more realistic setting, where a single fact is updated, as in knowledge editing or continual learning. The same relationship holds and the more the model still believes the true fact after training on the false one, the more misaligned it becomes. When we frame the same false fact as part of a coherent story, the model comes to believe it more deeply and becomes less misaligned than when we instruct it to assert the false fact. Content filters and persona vectors cannot tell these two framings apart, even though they lead to different levels of misalignment. These results suggest a risk for model updates, where training a model that does not adopt the new fact as true can induce misalignment even when the data looks harmless.
상세페이지_제목: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment

제목: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
저자: Zhenghao Li; Shengbo Wang; Nian Si
초록: Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $cμ$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $μ$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.
상세페이지_제목: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint

제목: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
저자: Lianmin Chen; Junbin Qiu; Chenxing Wei; Yao Shu; Kun He
초록: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization has emerged as a promising approach for memory-efficient large language model (LLM) post-training, yet its reliability in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) remains largely unexplored. Motivated by the distinct data regimes of on-policy RL and fixed-data optimization, we develop a generic variance-theoretic framework to investigate what limits the reliability of ZO gradient estimation. Our analysis reveals that estimation reliability is structurally determined by whether the two finite-difference evaluations are performed on matched data. On-policy reinforcement learning (RL) under the mismatched-data regime produces a $1/μ^2$ oracle-noise amplification that sets an irreducible noise floor as the perturbation scale $μ$ decreases, whereas Boltzmann Targeted SFT (BOLT) under the matched-data regime eliminates this amplification via noise cancellation. We further derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants that cleanly separate the two regimes. These results motivate the ZO-BOLT algorithm, which builds on BOLT's matched-data advantage for reliable ZO optimization of an RLVR-aligned objective. Controlled perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched end-to-end comparisons validate the predicted effect of data matching. Experiments across three models and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks further show that ZO-BOLT consistently improves over the pretrained baseline while retaining a near-inference memory footprint. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/lianmin-chen/the_cost_of_mismatch.
상세페이지_제목: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning

제목: Controlling Sharpening in LLM Post-Training
저자: Simon Matrenok; Nicolas Menet; Nicolas Flammarion; Andreas Krause
초록: LLM post-training via reinforcement learning has shown consistent improvements in accuracy at the cost of reducing behavioral coverage - a phenomenon known as sharpening that can stall progress on difficult tasks. Repeated sampling objectives such as $\mathrm{pass@k}$ and $\mathrm{max@k}$ are known to mitigate sharpening, but the mechanism behind it remains poorly understood. Moreover, existing approaches for $\mathrm{@k}$ optimization use dedicated algorithms, and no general framework exists for adapting established policy optimization methods from $\mathrm{@}1$ to $\mathrm{@k}$. We derive the optimal policies for KL-regularized $\mathrm{pass@k}$ and $\mathrm{max@k}$ objectives in closed form. Our explicit solutions reveal that $\mathrm{@k}$ optimization naturally redistributes learning pressure based on prompt difficulty, directing it toward harder problems. Crucially, we show that standard $\mathrm{@}1$ objectives achieve these exact same optimal policies through prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation. Ultimately, this yields an optimizer-independent explanation for why $\mathrm{@k}$ objectives reduce sharpening on easy tasks while prioritizing success on harder ones. Building on these insights, we introduce $\mathrm{@k}$ Adaptive Pressure for Policy Optimization (KAPPO). Following a one-time reference calibration, KAPPO seamlessly adapts existing $\mathrm{@}1$ methods to $\mathrm{@k}$ via prompt-adaptive regularization or reward transformation, without otherwise altering their training procedures. Experiments with several RL methods on mathematical reasoning and code generation demonstrate that KAPPO provides direct control over sharpening. Crucially, we demonstrate that $\mathrm{@k}$ pressure can be fully realized with single completion training, matching the performance of multi-completion $\mathrm{@k}$ optimizers at a fraction of the cost.
상세페이지_제목: Controlling Sharpening in LLM Post-Training

제목: Math Foundation Formalization Agent: A General-Purpose Approach to Formalizing Mathematical Foundations
저자: Jiaxin Xie; Guowei Dou; Xiang Ji; Wensheng Yu
초록: Mathematical formalization plays an important role in establishing rigorous and machine-verifiable foundations for mathematical reasoning. With the development of large language models (LLMs) and interactive theorem provers, intelligent agents offer a promising approach to automating the formalization of mathematical theories. This paper presents the Math Foundation Formalization Agent (MFF-Agent), a general-purpose intelligent agent designed to support formalization tasks across multiple mathematical domains. The agent integrates the reasoning capabilities of large language models with the formal verification capabilities of the Rocq proof assistant. It incorporates task classification, tool-assisted execution, verification feedback, and state-based task management to support the generation, refinement, and verification of formal proofs. Unlike an approach focused on a single mathematical theory, the agent is examined through case studies involving Morse--Kelley axiomatic set theory (MK), real numbers, propositional logic, and equivalences of the axiom of choice. These cases investigate its applicability across mathematical foundations and distinguish source-level completion, interactive verification, and reproducible compilation. The results demonstrate the feasibility of a unified operational framework for heterogeneous foundation-level tasks and clarify the gap between such a framework and a fully integrated mathematical foundation.
상세페이지_제목: Math Foundation Formalization Agent: A General-Purpose Approach to Formalizing Mathematical Foundations

제목: Graph-Based Testing of Conditional Mean Independence with Applications to Large Language Model Evaluation
저자: Mingshuo Liu; Qihua Zhu; Jingchi Liao; Lu Tian; Doudou Zhou
초록: We study whether a predictor $X$ provides additional information for predicting a scalar response $Y$ after adjustment for other variables $Z$, formalized by testing $\mathsf{H}_0:\E(Y\mid X,Z)=\E(Y\mid Z)$. Existing methods often require estimating nuisance functions involving $X$, which can be difficult for high-dimensional or structured predictors. We propose a graph-based test that extends the edge count principle to covariate adjustment. It represents $X$ through pairwise dissimilarities, estimates only the baseline regression $\E(Y\mid Z)$, and aggregates products of held-out residuals across graph edges. We develop sample-splitting and two-fold cross-fitting versions. Under regularity conditions, both have standard normal null limits, yielding analytic $p$-values, and are consistent under graph-smooth and graph-rough alternatives. Simulations with vector, image, and network predictors show good size control and power advantages over competing procedures, with cross-fitting improving power across the main alternatives. Applications examine human quality ratings, mathematical error labels, and LLM response preferences. Our method detects associations with quality ratings and an LLM judge's preferences after adjustment for text length and other recorded characteristics.
상세페이지_제목: Graph-Based Testing of Conditional Mean Independence with Applications to Large Language Model Evaluation

제목: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve
저자: Xujun Che; Depeng Xu; Jian Xiang; Taufiqua Khan
초록: The kernel of the Lean proof assistant checks that a proof establishes its statement. Whether the statement says what was intended is left to human reviewers. This is the old problem of validating a specification, and it grows more pressing as language models write formal statements in bulk and agents edit formal developments continuously. We present ProofPatch, a tool that helps reviewers judge Lean statements and keeps their judgments valid while the development changes. A reviewer can ask the kernel targeted questions about a statement, such as whether a hypothesis is needed or whether a counterexample exists. Each decision is stored with fingerprints of the statement as Lean elaborated it and of the definitions it depends on, and any declaration can be pinned so that a patch changing it is blocked, whether a person or an agent built on a large language model (LLM) wrote the patch. Working on elaborated terms rather than source text is the central design choice: notation and formatting changes leave a decision intact, and a changed definition reaches every theorem that uses it. On 229 pairs of consecutive revisions of Mathlib, Lean's mathematics library, ProofPatch sends 118 of 12,898 synthetic decisions back for review. Every text-based alternative misses at least 38 of these or sends back at least 13 times as many. On 1,527 labeled statements, kernel evidence flags unfaithful ones with precision 0.88 to 0.96, and in 344 runs of an LLM agent no change to a pinned statement got through.
상세페이지_제목: ProofPatch: Reviewing Lean Statements and Keeping the Reviews Valid as Formalizations Evolve

제목: Rethinking LLM Pruning via Test-Time Scaling
저자: Mingyang Song; Mao Zheng
초록: Structured pruning reduces the size of large language models, often at the cost of lower accuracy. Whether this decline reflects diminished reasoning capacity or greater difficulty in sampling correct solutions is less clear. We examine this question across expert, FFN and layer pruning on four mathematical and coding benchmarks, comparing original and pruned models through pass@k at matched sampling budgets. Even after substantial pruning, some models match or exceed the original model's reasoning coverage despite lower pass@1, and solve problems left unsolved in the original samples. Retaining broad coverage, however, does not mean that correct solutions remain easy to obtain. Under severe pruning, diverse generated chain-of-thought (CoT) traces can coexist with increased repetition and less reliable generation. As correct answers become harder to sample, the additional attempts can sharply increase total token use even when individual responses become shorter. This separation between coverage and sampling efficiency also clarifies expert-selection gains, as methods with markedly different pass@1 can solve the same problems at large budgets yet require different numbers of attempts to reach a common coverage target. Pruning should therefore be assessed by both the range of problems a model can still solve and the sampling cost of obtaining correct solutions.
상세페이지_제목: Rethinking LLM Pruning via Test-Time Scaling

제목: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
저자: Haozhan Tang; Hao Kang; Meng Lu; Yecheng Wu; Zerui Wang; Seokho Han; Haocheng Xi; Shuo Yang; Song Han; Han Cai
초록: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two BF16 pages per sequence and layer address quantization error; FP8 prefill uses a temporary arena while the persistent cache is packed directly from BF16 activations. Across four hybrid LLMs, a budget of 128 blocks per KV head shows no detected accuracy loss on the evaluated mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks, although some smaller budgets incur losses. With 64 blocks, Qwen3.8-27B achieves a $1.94\times$ end-to-end decode speedup over dense BF16 at 128K context and batch size 16 on one GB300, and the measured Qwen KV pools provide $2.58$-$2.76\times$ BF16's token capacity.
상세페이지_제목: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention

제목: Log-Driven Semantic Tuning for Mixed Integer Programming Solvers
저자: Zhengzhong Ricky You; Kaizhao Sun; Zeping Min; Wotao Yin; Xinshang Wang
초록: Automated configuration of mixed-integer programming (MIP) solvers largely relies on black-box optimization. Each trial requires an expensive solver run and provides only a scalar outcome, so tuning can require many such evaluations. Human experts take a different approach. They inspect solver logs, identify performance bottlenecks, and adjust the parameters that address them. We propose Log-Driven Semantic Tuning (LDST), which uses a large language model (LLM) to automate this process. LDST extracts compact diagnostics from solver logs, uses the LLM to propose sparse edits to the current best configuration based on parameter meanings and observed solver behavior, and validates each proposal before execution. A regime-adaptive objective selects the tuning signal according to the information available from a time-limited run, while a log-based completion signal estimates completion time from branch-and-bound tree growth recorded in ordinary solver logs, so that solved and unsolved runs share one time scale. On 215 instances from five benchmark sets, LDST reduces geometric-mean loss by 43.9% on easy instances and 16.7% on intermediate instances relative to the best of SMAC3, RBFOpt, and random search. In both regimes, LDST achieves a lower loss with 10 proposals than any of these baselines achieves with 50. Configurations that LDST tunes on a single instance also transfer better than baseline configurations to unseen instances of the same family.
